Beyoncé topped the Forbes list for the highest-earning musician of 2013-2014, amassing $115 million, thanks to her self-titled album release, 95 shows, and endorsement deals, with Taylor Swift, Pink, Rihanna, and Katy Perry following in that order. Other high-profile artists like Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys didn't make the top 10.

The Scottish National Party argues that it has 54 MPs compared to 40 Labour MPs who have expressed support for Jeremy Corbyn, but Speaker John Bercow maintains that Labour remains the official opposition due to parliamentary rules, despite challenges to Corbyn's leadership.

Villagers in Crickhowell successfully launch their own bid to purchase The Corn Exchange, aiming to transform it into independent shops and flats, after Punch Taverns halted their plans following local protests.

RIT Capital officially declines to make a formal bid for Alliance Trust, ending informal merger talks, and steps out of official takeover and mergers procedures, while Alliance Trust continues its fundamental review which could potentially result in a sale, outsourcing investment, or a deal, following changes in strategy initiated by activist investors to reduce the company's stock discount.

A former Police Community Support Officer, Alexis Scott, was convicted of six counts of theft and misfeasance for tricking passengers into believing they had too much cash on them when boarding flights at the North Terminal in April 2013, targeting long-haul passengers and taking around £13,500 from them, which Sussex Police later reimbursed. The judge criticized her use of her uniform and status to commit these offenses, expressing concern for the impact on the public trust and international reputation of the country.

Educational platform TrueTube has been nominated for three Bafta Awards, with category nominations for best drama, secondary learning, and drama for the film "Refugee." The comedy series Horrible Histories has earned three nominations for its Shakespeare special. The awards ceremony will take place at the Roundhouse in London on 20 November. Other nominees include The Amazing World of Gumball, Hetty Feather, The Dog Ate My Homework, Zootropolis, The Good Dinosaur, The Jungle Book, and Star Wars: The Force Awakens.

Lady Mary Soames, the last child of Sir Winston Churchill, bequeathed most of her art collection to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. Key paintings like Coast Scene near Cannes (1935) and View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club, 1946 will be displayed in these locations. The collection, which also includes Churchill's works and a painting of him at his easel, was accepted in lieu of inheritance tax. Culture Minister Ed Vaizey emphasized the significance of showcasing Churchill's artistic talent, as it offers an insight into his personal life beyond his political career.

The arrest of a former ombudsman employee is under investigation for potentially leaking sensitive documents containing information that could put lives at risk. The PSNI has launched a criminal investigation, and there are calls for police to be involved earlier in such cases to ensure independence and fairness. The police have suspended the sharing of sensitive material with the ombudsman's office until a review of security protocols is carried out.

Phyllis Schlafly, a conservative activist who opposed feminism, Communism, and the Equal Rights Amendment, played a significant role in shaping the political landscape of the 1970s and 1980s, and was credited for creating a climate favorable to Ronald Reagan's presidency. She championed traditional family values and was described as a patriot, a champion for women, and a symbol of strength by Donald Trump upon her death.

23-year-old rugby player, who played for Bristol, has decided to leave the team at the end of the season to return to Wales and further develop his skills, primarily as a full-back, with the hope of gaining more attention from the Wales national team.

The article describes the trial of the people smugglers accused of transporting the Syrian family, including three-year-old Alan Kurdi, who tragically died attempting to cross to Greece, resulting in a global focus on the refugee crisis. The smugglers were found not guilty of causing death through deliberate negligence but were convicted of people smuggling. The Kurdi family's story continues to emphasize the ongoing migrant crisis, with thousands of refugees and migrants arriving daily in Greece from Turkey.

Former Milan station chief Robert Lady, convicted in absentia in 2009 for his role in the 2003 abduction and extraordinary rendition of an Egyptian cleric, was reportedly arrested in Panama despite international search warrants sought by Italy's previous government in December 2012. Two of the 26 convicted individuals have had some contact with their lawyers, while none of them have appeared in an Italian court. The practice of extraordinary rendition, moving suspects to countries where torture is permitted, has been widely condemned by human rights groups.

Passenger traffic increased at Edinburgh and Glasgow airports in January 2017, with Edinburgh reporting an 11.7% year-on-year increase, and Glasgow seeing an 8.4% rise. International flights in particular saw significant growth at both airports. Meanwhile, Aberdeen International Airport recorded its lowest decline in passenger numbers in nearly two years, but still saw a decrease of 1.7%. The article also mentions the growth of EU-scheduled traffic at Glasgow Airport, the increase in domestic traffic at both Edinburgh and Glasgow airports, and the commencement of new flights at Aberdeen Airport by Ryanair and Loganair.
The record-breaking video "Gangnam Style" by Psy has amassed over 9 quintillion views on YouTube, forcing the platform to update its video counter limitations.
England aim to secure a spot in the World Twenty20 semi-finals, with key player Alex Hales possibly returning from injury for their match against Sri Lanka.

Scotland's two largest cities, Edinburgh and Glasgow, rank second and third respectively among Britain's most congested cities, with anticipated costs of £2.8bn and £2.3bn in wasted time for Edinburgh and Glasgow drivers respectively over the next decade due to traffic congestion. If unaddressed, congestion levels across the UK could cost £61.8bn by 2025, with London having the most traffic "pinch points" in Europe, according to a study by Inrix Roadway Analytics.

In the 44th minute, Norway's Nordtveit scored an unexpected goal against Northern Ireland as his shot deflected off Sammy Clingan's heel, while in the second half, substitutes Elyounoussi, Ruud, and O'Neill's team contributed to Norway's 3-0 victory. Northern Ireland struggled to score, even during a frantic goalmouth scramble before half-time, and have not won more than one friendly in their last 14 matches.

Brussels remains on high alert due to fears of Paris-style attacks, with hundreds of armed police and soldiers patrolling the city. Authorities have arrested five people in Belgium in connection to the Paris attacks, and an arrest warrant has been issued for Mohamed Abrini. Abdelhamid Abaaoud, the suspected ringleader of the Paris attacks who was killed in police raids in Saint Denis, is believed to have been near the Bataclan theatre during the siege, and had connections to the attacks. President Hollande and President Obama have reiterated their commitment to eradicating IS.

There were coordinated terrorist attacks in Zaventem Airport, Brussels, and Maalbeek metro station that resulted in 31 deaths and numerous injuries, with the Islamic State group claiming responsibility; resulting in a call for calmness and solidarity, with increased security measures worldwide.

Sheffield City Council has served a legal notice to Green Party Councillor, Alison Teal, threatening a High Court injunction for her continued involvement in tree-felling protests, citing months of alleged unlawful disruption to a 25-year tree management program, aimed at ensuring a better street scene and diverse tree stock.

Hundreds of whales have stranded at Farewell Spit, South Island, New Zealand, with many deaths; efforts to save survivors are ongoing, including the formation of a human chain to refloat them. This is one of the largest mass beachings in New Zealand, and the country has one of the highest stranding rates in the world. Experts suggest that shallow waters at the location confuse whales and hinder their ability to navigate.

The Welsh rugby union team Ospreys have signed experienced prop forward Brian Mujati as injury cover for the sidelined Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, with Rhodri Jones also unavailable due to Wales Six Nations duty. Mujati, who has played at top levels in Super Rugby, France's Top 14, and England's Premiership, is expected to provide valuable experience and bolster the squad during the remaining PRO12 games and Challenge Cup quarter-final.

The Gwynedd council plans to establish a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, despite 500 residents opposing the move and a previous dispute involving the church's support for the project. A report on the matter will be discussed at the council's cabinet meeting on 14th February, with the new three-to-19 campus expected to open in September 2018.

The article discusses Oxfordshire County Council's proposal to have one organization running all services, opposed by district councils who argue for either a mayor or three separate councils. The debate is criticized as a "turf war" over devolution plans, with arguments focusing on efficiency, representation, and the needs of different communities within the county. No independent studies or specific cuts to local services are mentioned, and residents are currently being asked for their opinions on the proposals.

The Edinburgh rugby team is battling a challenging schedule, attempting to secure a top-four finish in the league, with a demanding series of five matches against the Newport Gwent Dragons, Zebre, Leinster, Munster, and Cardiff Blues, feeling it's essential to secure victories in all to maintain playoff contention, contending that errors and a loss of momentum after Six Nations break have impacted their recent results.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group is rescuing and nursing back to health bat pups abandoned due to challenging weather conditions and releasing them back into the wild, debunking misconceptions about the animals' role in controlling pests and contributing to agriculture.

The Supreme Court is currently considering a case regarding federal law limiting gun ownership for individuals convicted of domestic violence, with Justice Clarence Thomas inquiring if the violation of any law suspends a person's constitutional rights.

Responsible Travel, a wildlife holiday specialist, is dropping about half a dozen trips involving zoos from their 3,500 options, as their boss, Justin Francis, finds these zoos inhumane and outdated, following the influence of a BBC TV program. The majority of the targeted zoos are in southeast Asia and none are in the UK. The decision is supported by the Born Free Foundation, which argues that animals often develop abnormal behavior in captivity and a global shift could significantly reduce the exploitation of wild animals in zoos worldwide.

A primary school-age child was found dead, leading to a 40-year-old woman's arrest on suspicion of murder in Faringdon, UK. Police are increasing their presence in the area as a precaution, seeking public assistance, and asking anyone with information to contact them.

A suspect in the UK is accused of breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim), reportedly the first such alleged violation, with the suspect alleged to have failed to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station twice in January. The Home Office refused to comment on the case, and those subject to a TPim can be ordered to report daily to a police station and adhere to other restrictions, with some arguing that TPims have weakened public protection against terrorism. The suspect has been granted unconditional bail, and the case is set for a plea and case management hearing on July 2.

Qualcomm, the world's largest chip supplier for smartphones, will reduce royalty rates on patents used in China's mobile phone market following a ruling that it violated the country's anti-monopoly law. The move could potentially benefit Chinese smartphone manufacturers Xiaomi and Huawei, as Qualcomm now charges royalties based on 65% of the selling price of phones in China instead of the entire price. The company, which made about half its global revenue in China, increased its profit and revenue forecast for the current fiscal year following the agreement.

Michelle Mellotte, 61, a former doctor, was found guilty of fraud by abusing her role in 2010 when she took a £10,000 loan from an Alzheimer's patient, Michael McGrory, promising to return it but failing to do so. Following an investigation, the loan was returned, and Mellotte was suspended and later removed from the medical register. The Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service concluded that Mellotte posed a risk to patients, brought the profession into disrepute, breached fundamental tenets of the profession, and her integrity could not be relied upon, effectively ending her ability to practice as a doctor in the UK.

A skeleton of a man aged between 30 and 49 years old, wearing a specific brand of clothing from 2008, was discovered at the M54 motorway in Shropshire, England. Police are unable to determine the cause of death and are not ruling out the possibility of a crime having occurred.

Archaeologists have discovered a previously unknown stone "square megalithic monument" at Avebury, one of Europe's largest stone circles, which is thought to be one of the site's earliest structures and potentially commemorates the ancestral home of the first people living in Avebury.

The article discusses a petition by hospital staff and residents opposing a proposed parking scheme in Reading, England, due to concerns it will exacerbate parking pressures, especially for hospital staff and patients, and make living in the area difficult. The council plans to install charges and restrictions on 625 parking spaces, with further consultation sought from residents before a decision is made.

US Navy personnel, under increased scrutiny due to a series of incidents, are facing stricter alcohol policies and training following a three-car accident involving Petty Officer Aimee Mejia in Okinawa, which injured two people and resulted in Mejia's arrest for allegedly driving under the influence. The US military, which is heavily present in Okinawa and faces longstanding opposition from locals, has co-operated with the Japanese investigation and expressed sympathy for the victims. The incident, which happened during a period of mourning for another alleged crime, has sparked renewed outrage among Okinawans and Japanese authorities.

A pair of young English batsmen, Duckett and Bell-Drummond, set the second highest List A partnership record of 367 runs, helping the Lions beat Sri Lanka A in a tri-series where they also defeated both Pakistan A and Sri Lanka A twice each. Their performances have caught the attention of coach Andy Flower, with Duckett's 220 not out being the ninth-highest List A score and Malan scoring 185 in another win, while Billings contributed a 175. Flower is optimistic that these players could have successful international careers.

The article states that Colombia's peace talks, suspended after rebels kidnapped Gen Ruben Dario Alzate and two others on 16 November, will resume in Havana from 10 December, with a focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victims' families, and aim to end five decades of conflict in which 220,000 people are estimated to have died. The captives were released and reunited with their families, and Gen Alzate resigned following the incident.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign organized a protest March in Oxford against Oxfordshire County Council's plans to cut 44 children's centres and replace them with eight "children and family centres", with the goal of saving Â£8m. David Cameron was invited to join the protest, but the government spokesperson responded by saying that the government continues to work with councils to make back-office savings in order to protect frontline services.

A controversial sandcastle depicting a murdered woman surrounded by police tape, constructed by Devon and Cornwall Police at a family beach event, was criticized as being offensive and insensitive due to its sexual stereotyping and trivialization of serious matters, particularly the reporting of sex crimes. The police apologized for any offense caused.

Leyton Orient's manager, Slade, has revealed plans for a revised club structure post-takeover and is eager to strengthen the squad, despite financially modest ambitions, with the goal of improving on last season's performance and challenging for promotion.

In the Scottish Open tournament, English golfer Tom Hatton earned a spot at both The Open Championship and the USPGA Championship, achieved his best European Tour finish of second place, and earned a substantial payday despite a few missed birdie opportunities. Tom Hatton is teeing off with Harold Varner III and Oskar Arvidsson.

The 10-year-old Many Clouds, owned by Trevor Hemmings and known for its successful racing history, tragically died of a severe pulmonary haemorrhage after narrowly winning the Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham's Festival Trials Day, despite previously receiving treatment for a tendency to 'overheat' and showing no symptoms of post-race ataxia on the day of the race. The British Horseracing Authority is determined to investigate what causes such symptoms and potential prevention measures.

A 12-year-old witness testified in court that she was abused and later raped in Blackpool by Basharat Hussain and several other men, seven individuals including Hussain are on trial over alleged child abuse in Rotherham from 1987 to 2003, accused of targeting and exploiting children.

A 32-year-old motorcycle racer, Franck Petricola, tragically died at the TT after making a successful comeback from a serious accident at last year's North West 200. He was the 141st fatality at the races since they started in 1907, and an investigation is underway following the incident. Known for his resilience, Petricola had suffered multiple fractures and a head injury in a crash at the North West 200 in 2014 and had made a full recovery to compete at this year's event just last month.

Guy Martin, a popular racer, will not be returning to the Isle of Man TT due to a crash and mechanical issues with his Honda machine. Despite this, the event promises an exciting season with strong performances expected from Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, Dean Harrison, and other potential dark horses.

The article describes a disaster situation in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, following torrential rain flooding the area, resulting in the evacuation and rescue of more than 20,000 people, numerous road, home and infrastructure blockages, and thousands forced to seek shelter. The region has a history of dealing with extreme weather events, including a 2011 flood incident and the catastrophic impact of Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

US Soccer plans to limit heading for players aged 11-13, introduce new safety guidelines, and modify substitution rules in relation to concussions following a lawsuit, while the Football Association in England is considering new guidelines for managing head injuries. The FA is also working with an independent expert panel to identify research questions on the long-term effects of head injuries on the brain.

Jerome Lavrilleux, a deputy director of former President Nicolas Sarkozy's 2012 presidential campaign, claimed Sarkozy was not directly involved in allegations of sometimes fluid finances involving potentially millions of euros worth of fake invoices, attributing the problem to a lack of oversight and warning of potential complications for any future election attempts by Sarkozy. The allegations were made by Patrick Maisonneuve, the lawyer for event organiser Bygmalion, who claimed that the UMP ordered fake invoices to cover overspends during the campaign. The scandal could potentially harm the UMP party and complicate any future election bids by Sarkozy.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) reported a decrease in home repossessions in the second quarter of the year, with 2,500 homes repossessed compared to 3,000 in the previous quarter and 5,400 in the same quarter last year. The decline was attributed to low interest rates, but the CML advised homeowners to prepare for a potential increase in interest rates. The number of homeowners and landlords in arrears also decreased, while the number of tenant evictions by landlords rose by 4%. Shelter cautioned that rising rents and welfare cuts were contributing to families losing their homes.

The article details that the city accepted 105 Syrian refugees between October and March as part of the UK's expanded resettlement programme, with costs covered by the UK Government. While this generated some controversy among politicians like UKIP MEP James Carver who claimed it put undue pressure on services in Coventry compared to other areas, local authorities overall showed a "tremendous amount of goodwill". Notably, none of the refugees were placed in the North West, and only three were settled in areas such as Kingston upon Thames and Mid Sussex. The Home Office plans to resettle 20,000 Syrian refugees by 2020 as part of its Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme.

Brazil's President Dilma Rousseff plans for the Olympic torch relay, which will be carried out by thousands of torchbearers in 300 Brazilian cities leading up to the 2016 Games in Rio de Janeiro. She has also reassured concerned athletes about water pollution in Guanabara Bay, stating that water pollution will not pose a major health risk during the Olympics.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's electoral reform, passed by the lower house of parliament, seeks to end Italy's era of revolving governments and political horse-trading by awarding a majority of seats to the party winning the most votes in an election. The reform also includes proposals to abolish the Senate. Critics argue that the law may reduce voter choice and give too much power to political parties. The reform needs approval from the upper house of parliament to come into force.

The 20-year-old Ajax footballer, Abdelhak Nouri, is diagnosed with severe brain damage following heart rhythm problems during a game in Austria, with the prognosis for recovery being grim, according to a club statement.

Swansea earned a crucial win, following a string of losses, in a match where Jordan Ayew scored for Villa Park but was answered by Sigurdsson's free-kick and a winning goal by Jordan's brother, Andre. This victory lifted Swansea out of a slump, providing improved morale and adding confidence in preparation for their home game against Arsenal.

A Polish mother is requesting help from Costa coffee shop customers and employees to locate her 10-year-old son who has been missing since early this year, as he is believed to be in the UK with his British father and often frequented Costa coffee shops, and her legal representative is appealing for information to ensure the boy's safety and reunite him with his mother.

New US travel rules require dual citizens from certain countries, including Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Sudan, to apply for a visa at the US embassy instead of using the visa waiver scheme. The changes have caused confusion and controversy, particularly for those who gained their second nationality through marriage or parentage, and have sparked widespread anger and disproportionate impact concerns.

Sky is working to increase capacity at affected telephone exchanges to address issues with slow internet speeds, potentially caused by an increase in network traffic and a high rate of new customer additions. The problem has been particularly seen in areas like Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol, but a postcode checking facility has been provided for subscribers to check if their local exchange has been flagged as having an issue. The issue seems to be related to Sky's promotional activities, which may have attracted subscribers who consume significantly more data than the average UK broadband user.

A Liverpool gang led by Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan was convicted for a series of ATM robberies in Scotland between August and November 2013. The gang, using explosives to access safes behind the ATMs, was responsible for incidents in multiple towns and thefts totaling over £133,000. The gang's activities spread across Stonehaven, Inverurie, Aberdeen, New Deer, and Ellon, and they were found guilty of blowing up cash machines at various locations, as well as attempting to steal from ATMs and stealing property from a golf shop. Sentences were deferred for the duo, Rob Vaughan admitted to participating in the crimes, while McHale and Schruyers were also found guilty of attempting to break into an ATM in Mintlaw. The investigation ultimately traced the group to Liverpool due to the circulation of Scottish banknotes with telltale signs of dye in the Mersey area.

The Scottish Prison Service has announced the use of new technology to interfere with mobile phone signals at two pilot sites (HMP Shotts and Glenochil) as part of efforts to combat the use of contraband phones, which have been linked to criminal activities such as drug supply, organized crime, and harassment. The technology is expected to become operational within weeks and could serve as a model for future installations.

Former French President Francois Hollande attended a ceremony to mark 70 years since the liberation of the last Nazi camps, emphasizing the importance of knowledge in preventing future atrocities. The commemorations also included events in Germany and Croatia, mourning the loss of thousands at Bergen-Belsen and Jasenovac, while acknowledging the ongoing social and religious tensions, particularly those affecting Jews and Muslims.

Johnny Depp, 52, and Amber Heard, 30, have filed for divorce in Los Angeles Superior Court, citing irreconcilable differences after 15 months of marriage. The celebrity couple, who have no children, have recently faced court proceedings in Australia over allegations of illegal dog importation, resulting in a war of words spanning months, including disputes about the dogs' welfare and insults such as Depp calling Deputy Prime Minister Barnaby Joyce "inbred with a tomato."

The Maersk Tigris, a container ship, remains anchored off Bandar Abbas in Iranian waters, despite being in international shipping lanes, due to a seizure reportedly based on a court order over a debt dispute with a private Iranian company, causing distress among its 24 East Asian and Eastern European crew members, which includes a British national but no Americans. US Naval Forces Central Command has received the ship's distress signal and have dispatched a destroyer and a reconnaissance plane to monitor the situation, criticizing the IRGC Navy's approach and warning shots.

The article discusses a call made by Sarah Pollock, seeking the disclosure of the full Seren Bernard case review report from 2014, which details her tragic suicide while in foster care in 2012. Despite a personal request and the report's intended purpose as a "document for learning," the Pembrokeshire council was unable to disclose the full report based on "clear legal advice," leaving Ms. Pollock feeling traumatized and seeking continued efforts to make the report public.

In a Super League game, Leigh defeated Salford 24-0, with 18 points scored in the first half and further extension in the second. This win relegated Widnes Vikings to the bottom of the table. Meaning Salford, who ended the regular season in fourth place, missed out on their highest league finishing position in 40 years. Both coaches praised the opposing team and emphasized the need for improvement moving forward.

Paul Allen and Burt Rutan, aided by Elon Musk's space company, are building a gigantic aircraft capable of launching unmanned rockets into space, offering launch flexibility, minimizing weather constraints, and saving rocket fuel, with potential applications for the commercial satellite industry and the International Space Station.

In a tight first-class cricket match, Lancashire amassed a challenging total of 364, thanks in part to a crucial partnership by Ashwell Prince and Steven Croft and a late push by wicketkeeper Alex Davies (89). Derbyshire began their response struggling at 27-2, with openers Ben Slater and Billy Godleman dismissed by Peter Siddle and Tom Bailey respectively. Davies expressed confidence in his team's abilities to defend the total, while Tom Taylor, despite noting the potential for his team to achieve victory, recognized the importance of forming big partnerships and contributions from all players.

Jon Stewart, a renowned American satirist and the voice of liberal America, concluded his 17-year stint as host of The Daily Show, with guests such as Bruce Springsteen, John Kerry, and John McCain in attendance. His final monologue expressed gratitude to colleagues, fans, and family, emphasizing that the show was not ending but pausing, and departing with a quip about getting a drink. The Daily Show, which has been influential for young viewers, has launched the careers of several famous comedians, including Steve Carell, John Oliver, and Stephen Colbert, among others. #JonVoyage trended on Twitter as fans, including McCain, paid tribute to Stewart as he bid farewell.

Forest, who have failed to advance past the third round of the cup competition in the past 11 seasons, aim to qualify again and potentially secure a spot in the Europa League, starting their campaign against League Two side Doncaster.

The Arches nightclub, a significant cultural venue in Glasgow, went into administration after a midnight closing time was imposed due to drug abuse and disorder incidents, putting 130 jobs at risk. The Scottish government has pledged support, with Creative Scotland providing immediate funding and exploring long-term options, and is calling for collaboration between the city council, police, and management to find a solution.

In 1972, Jean McConville, a mother-of-10, was kidnapped by the IRA, accused of being an informant, and was later found dead in 2003. On Tuesday, Ivor Bell, a senior IRA leader in the 1970s, was arrested for aiding and abetting her murder and membership of the IRA. He was part of a delegation that held secret talks with the British government in 1972, including Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness. McConville is one of the "Disappeared," those abducted, murdered, and secretly buried by republicans during the Troubles, and the IRA admitted to this in 1999. An Independent Commission for the Location of Victims' Remains, established in 1999, is still searching for the remains of seven of the disappeared.

Wigan Warriors overcame a 12-man disadvantage to score 21 unanswered points, beating Catalans Dragons, strengthening their confidence for the remainder of the season while their league leaders' shield prospects remain dependent on Warrington's upcoming game against Hull FC.

The Yorkshire Sculpture Park has seen a massive 170% increase in visitor numbers during September due to the installation of the poppy sculpture "Wave," attracting 100,000 people compared to 37,000 last year. This Nationwide Tour production is a segment from the Bloom Swept Lands and Seas of Red artwork, and the park anticipates a record-breaking year with over half a million visitors feeling it provides a unique, contemplative experience.

A severe flood warning on the A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was lifted on March 10th following inspections and clearance work, despite some remaining water on the road, temporary traffic lights were installed. Local authorities thanked their teams for their efforts, urging caution due to filled-up rhynes and foggy conditions. The A372 Langport Road remains closed for flood pump removal next week, while the large pumps at Beer Wall are no longer needed due to improving weather. After pump removal, the road will close for further flood damage assessment and emergency repairs.

Scientists have discovered a distant object, V774104, estimated to be between 500-1,000 kilometers across and likely 15.5 billion kilometers from the Sun using Japan's Subaru telescope. The team behind the discovery is led by Scott Sheppard and Chad Trujillo, who specialize in detecting Solar System outliers. V774104 is significantly further out than Pluto and its orbital trajectory remains uncertain compared to other distant objects in the Solar System like Eris, Voyager 1, 2012 VP113, and Sedna.

A primary school headteacher, Ashley Yates, has admitted to using a spy pen to record indecent images of children and staff at The Tynings Primary School, South Gloucestershire. Further investigations have uncovered additional adult victims. Police continue their enquiries and Yates remains in custody until his next court hearing on 9th August. School officials are working closely with authorities to provide information and support to those affected.

British rowers Helen Glover and Heather Stanning, unbeaten in 39 races, won the women's rowing event in Rio with a time of 7:18.29, setting a new Olympic record and finishing 1.2 seconds ahead of New Zealand to become double Olympic champions.

Steve and Ola, a presenter and dance partner on Strictly Come Dancing, admit that they were misread in a bullying allegation and maintained their unity and professionalism throughout the incident. They found it challenging but handled it by maintaining a positive attitude and focusing on their dance performances. They also encourage people affected by bullying to seek help.

Inflation dropped from 2.9% to 2.6% in June, reducing expectations for a rate hike, which saw the pound depreciate (against both the dollar and euro), initially boosting the FTSE 100 due to reduced sterling strength, but closing down 13.91 points, with Royal Mail shares rising 3% due to increased revenues.

Nottingham-born actress Vicky McClure, famously recognized by her tram on the Nottingham city network, shared an uncomfortable story on The Graham Norton Show about her tram ride in 2015. She and her mother were offered a free ride after a ceremony to unveil the tram, but later challenged by a conductor. Despite presenting the plaque she received at the ceremony, the pair were thrown off for fare evasion, though Nottingham Express Transit acknowledged it was an "unfortunate misunderstanding."

The inquest examines the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross in West London, looking into potential failures by the government and police that could have contributed to her death, and considering the circumstances that allowed arrested murder convict Arnis Zalkalns to live freely in the UK. Alice's mother, Rosalind Hodgkiss, expressed shock at Zalkalns' presence in the country and called for improvements in monitoring foreign offenders and cross-border information sharing to prevent similar incidents in the future. Alice was a vibrant and popular young woman with a keen interest in songwriting; the full circumstances of her death, discovered a month after she went missing along the canal, are still unclear.

The study by The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling indicates that the average retail vacancy rate in Scotland has decreased slightly to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest rate (33%) and Inverurie the lowest (1%). The research also shows that around 40% of empty shops in Scotland have been vacant for over three years, with leisure businesses increasing significantly as a presence in cities and towns. The study identifies the towns with the best and worst vacancy rates and highlights that in many towns, nearly 40% of the vacant units have been vacant for over three years, which is a major barrier to healthy and sustainable communities.

Rory McWhirter, from Edinburgh, created false identities by deceiving people into applying for nonexistent jobs at a Glasgow hotel and used these identities to produce falsified birth certificates, which he then used to claim significant amounts in tax credits, child benefits, and a Sure Start maternity grant. His scheme was exposed when he was recognized at the Aberdeen registry office, and he was subsequently convicted of fraud. His attorney argued for leniency due to his income and failed business ventures, but Sheriff Alastair Carmichael sentenced McWhirter to jail for his complex and threatening fraudulent scheme against public finance, vital records, and the benefits system.

The authorities in Saudi Arabia have been trying to demolish the old Shia quarter of Awamiya since May, with activists alleging that this effort is to forcibly displace residents, while accusing security forces of firing randomly at homes and cars, resulting in clashes that have left at least seven people dead. The region, where the majority are Shia, has been experiencing increased unrest since 2011, with protests and attacks becoming more frequent following the 2016 execution of a prominent Shia cleric.

The article discusses young adults in Belfast expressing frustration over the struggle to find employment, criticizing the election-focused behavior of politicians and calling for improved job opportunities, training programs, and political focus on issues beyond elections.

Andrew Travers, Barnet Council's Chief Executive, stepped down after a polling error led to the exclusion of voters in the borough during the EU Referendum, with an independent investigation launching to review the incident's appropriateness and make recommendations for future elections.

Manager Neil Warnock has extended an offer to midfielder Peter Whittingham for a new contract, allowing him time to consider it, while hinting that his long-term plans do not include Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe, who have since moved on loan.

The article discusses tennis player Jamie Fleming expressing concern over reported match-fixing in the tennis world, emphasizing the importance of maintaining sport's purity and fairness, and stating he has no knowledge of it in the Australian Open currently taking place.

A 60-year-old man walked into a bank on Bristol Road South in Northfield, reportedly producing a firearm without making any threats or demands. He was later taken to hospital for a psychiatric evaluation and is expected to be questioned about suspected firearms offences. Police contained the scene, negotiated with the man, and no customers or staff were harmed in the incident.

Mohammed Ali, a 31-year-old software programmer from Liverpool, has denied attempting to possess a deadly toxin (ricin) after allegedly ordering it online, pretending to be "Weirdos 0000." The supposed deal was actually a sting operation carried out by the FBI, who had been posing as the supplier. The trial is ongoing, with the defense suggesting Ali's actions were driven by his interest in pushing technological boundaries, possibly influenced by the TV series "Breaking Bad."

Newport County football club, tenants of Rodney Parade stadium, are facing criticism from rugby team manager Westley over the quality of the football pitch, which Davies, CEO of Rodney Parade Limited, states is being repaired but lacks a immediate solution due to high costs.

Nearly 7 out of 10 people surveyed admitted to working while unwell, with concerns about backlogged work upon return, while only a quarter admitted to taking sick days when healthy. The survey highlights the issue of presenteeism, where employees attend work ill, posing a potential threat to productivity and morale.

The Bank of England cut its growth forecast for 2017, held interest rates at 0.25%, and saw a disappointing performance from pharmaceuticals firm Hikma due to US regulatory delays on a new drug, while the FTSE 100 index closed slightly up, supported by mining shares.

Russian hacker and son of a Russian MP, Roman Seleznev, was found guilty of operating a credit card theft scheme targeting US pizza chains in Washington state between 2008 and 2014. He faces a mandatory four-year jail term, following the conviction on 38 out of 40 charges, including fraud and ID theft. Prosecutors considered him one of the most prolific credit card thieves in history, having stolen and sold nearly 3 million credit card numbers. The hacking involved infiltrating point-of-sale systems in pizza restaurants and installing malware to siphon off credit card numbers, which were then sold on net markets. Over 3,700 businesses were affected. Seleznev's legal team plans to appeal, challenging his 2014 arrest in the Maldives and the use of corrupted laptop evidence.

The president, under pressure to produce alleged recordings following an inquiry into Russian election interference and after he requested James Comey drop an investigation, denied their existence in a tweet. However, Comey had previously stated that he was asked by the president to let go of any possible prosecution of former National Security Adviser Mike Flynn and hinted he hopes there are recordings of their conversation.

Tata Steel's UK assets, including the Port Talbot factory, sites at Newport and Rotherham, and operations at Corby, Shotton and Teesside, are the target of a proposed takeover by Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, with a formal bid submission due on Tuesday. Macquarie Bank is advising Liberty and is a potential financial backer, while a management buyout team, Excalibur Steel UK Limited, led by former Tata executive Stuart Wilkie, is also planning to submit a bid. The UK government has pledged support for any potential buyer, and Tata's Scunthorpe operation has already been sold.

Nottingham area trams are planned to extend to East Midlands Airport, Toton's HS2 station, and potentially other cities like Derby, with local councils viewing it as a priority in devolution negotiations, although costs and timetables are not yet disclosed.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the five-time world champion, equalized Stephen Hendry's record for most Masters wins and recorded the biggest-ever margin of victory (9-0) in a Masters final by modifying his game, citing inspiration from young players like Neil Robertson, Judd Trump, and Ding Junhui, which boosts his self-belief and confidence.

Extremely destructive storms killed six people, damaged thousands of homes, and destroyed vast forests, including rare habitats, in Poland; officials estimate eight million cubic meters of lumber were lost, making it the worst forest disaster in Polish and possibly European history. The disaster occurred in the northern and western regions, with Torun alone losing over 23,000 hectares of forest. The Polish government faces intense criticism for logging in Europe's oldest forest, Bialowieza, a UNESCO World Heritage site that is home to rare wildlife. The European Court of Justice will determine the fate of ongoing logging operations in the coming months.

Singer Enrique Iglesias suffered a more extensive injury than initially assessed during a concert in Tijuana, Mexico, where he reached for a drone camera, requiring reconstructive surgery and a fracture correction; he is expected to resume his tour on July 3rd.

In the Super League match, Leeds Rhinos defeated Warrington Wolves 24-0 with Matt Parcell scoring a hat-trick and Joel Moon scoring his 15th try in 16 games. Warrington made numerous handling errors, and the closest they came to scoring was a Joe Philbin try that was held up over the line. Leeds head coach Brian McDermott commented on the performance, expressing satisfaction with the clean sheet but acknowledging that the team was playing a struggling Warrington side. Warrington head coach Tony Smith attributed the loss to poor execution, forcing mistakes, and weak kicking game.

William (Plum) Smith, a former paramilitary and PUP leader, played a central role in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, particularly by chairing a press conference for the Combined Loyalist Military Command. He was a key figure in bringing loyalist paramilitaries into the peace process and was noted for his intelligence, progressive political views, and efforts to represent working-class individuals. He passed away, with tributes paid by prominent figures such as Martin McGuinness and Brian Ervine.

Mrs Cooke, 92, of Bristol, has been a long-standing poppy seller for the Royal British Legion (RBL) for over 75 years, starting her involvement as a teenager. For the past 12 years, she has sold poppies at Bristol Cathedral's entrance, with a personal connection to the cause as her first husband was killed in action during World War II. The RBL deeply appreciates her dedication to the organization and the annual Poppy Appeal.

Israeli statesman Shimon Peres, a key figure in the founding of Israel and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate for his efforts in resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, passed away after a stroke at the age of 93. His political career spanned more than six decades and included roles as prime minister, president, and, early on, defense minister. Notable achievements include securing deals for arms and aircraft, founding Israel's nuclear facility, and overseeing the successful rescue of Israeli hostages held in Uganda. Late in his career, he advocated for peace with the Palestinians and continued his efforts through the Peres Centre for Peace.

The BBC reported that a major survey conducted at Queen's University in Northern Ireland, with over 70% participation, found that only 29% of staff agreed on effective leadership, while ratings were generally positive regarding change management, job satisfaction, university standing, and commitment to world-class research. However, staff were skeptical about change resulting from the survey. The university responded by acknowledging the survey results, emphasizing staff engagement, and committing to developing action plans to address challenges and build on identified strengths.

The X-47B jet, being developed by Northrop Grumman, had its maiden flight reaching an altitude of 5,000 feet for 29 minutes. Its tailless stealth design, similar to the B-2 Stealth Bomber, aims to create a new generation of radar-invisible, faster unmanned drones, different from current remote-controlled planes like the Predator and Reaper. The X-47B is part of a £395 million contract and is expected to undergo further tests, including its first one from an aircraft carrier in 2013.

Airbus announces reduced production of the double-deck A380 aircraft, acknowledges disappointing second-quarter profits, struggling with delays in US engine-maker Pratt & Whitney's engines for A320neo aircraft, and is having constructive talks with Qatar Airways over their recent cancellation of four A350 aircraft orders.

The Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea has experienced a 40% coral death rate, the highest in at least 40 years, according to expert Anne Cohen. Cohen attributes this to the 2015/2016 El Nino which caused devastating bleaching in several coral reefs globally, not just the Great Barrier Reef. The high local weather anomaly turned a predicted 2 degrees Celsius warming into an actual 6 degrees Celsius warming, leading to widespread coral death. Cohen suggests that predictions regarding the future of coral reefs may be overly optimistic for some shallow-water reefs, and that drastic action to reduce global warming is necessary to preserve these vital ecosystems.

Scientists at the University of Queensland and Monash University have developed a protein from Australian funnel-web spider venom, called Hi1a, which has shown promising results in reducing brain damage in laboratory rats during stroke simulations. While the research is still in its early stages, it could potentially lead to future treatments for stroke.

In a football match between Oldham and Bradford, Oldham took an early 1-0 lead through a header from a free-kick. Despite Bradford dominating the rest of the game, they were unable to take the lead and the score remained 1-0 at halftime. Bradford equalized via a penalty kick after a foul by Ousmane Fane, but were still unable to take the lead. The game ended in a 1-1 draw.

The article reports that a new drug, aducanumab, shows potential in slowing memory decline and reducing amyloid plaques in the brain, but concerns persist since larger studies are needed to fully evaluate its effects and side effects such as headaches have been experienced by some patients in the study.

In the Challenge Cup, Oldham Roughyeds, currently fourth from the bottom in the second tier, led 24-6 at halftime against Hull Kingston Rovers, a Super League side. Despite a comeback attempt by Hull KR in the second half, Oldham held on to win 24-22, making it one of the biggest wins since the club reformed in 1997. Hull KR's coach described their performance as an "utter embarrassment." The article does not provide the final score for the game but supports that Oldham won the match against Hull KR.

The BBC director general, Lord Hall, plans to develop a children's iPlayer, a network of local reporters, an Ideas Service, and the opportunity for third-party content on the iPlayer, subject to funding cuts and potential criticism from the Scottish Newspaper Society and the News Media Association over concerns of undermining local news publishing.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission, in a letter to party leaders, expresses concern over increasing hate attacks in the UK since the Brexit vote, calling for accurate information and respectful debate. It points to a rise in hate crimes, including the murder of Jo Cox, racist, anti-Semitic, and homophobic attacks, and the pulling off of hijabs, as "stains on our society". The commission urges all politicians to be mindful of their impact on national mood and suggests reviewing hate crime sentences in England and Wales.

A suspended UKIP member, Ms. Evans, is unable to run for leadership due to opposition from high-ranking party members. She has criticized the party's leadership and advocates for internal reform, a shift towards the center-ground to break free from a hard-right image, and a unified politics rather than a divisive group. She endorses Lisa Duffy as the best candidate for leading this transformation within UKIP. Ms. Evans previously wrote the party's 2015 general election manifesto but was removed from her policy role in party infighting.

The changes to the English GCSE system will involve a new grading system using numbers instead of letters, scrapping coursework for most subjects, and returning to two-year linear assessments. This will initially apply to English language, English literature, maths, and start from the autumn of 2015. Other popular GCSE subjects will follow suit by 2018. Scotland and Northern Ireland will not be affected, while Wales is planning its own GCSE shake-up. The new system aims to raise expectations and improve core skills in English and maths, but there are concerns about the potential negative impact on less able students and the confusion caused by the blend of numbered and traditional letter grades.

Gen. Petraeus, who resigned as CIA director in 2012 due to an extramarital affair and served as a senior officer under Presidents Bush and Obama, stated his willingness to serve under President Trump and suggested potential closeness with Russia, drawing a parallel to previous diplomatic outreach.

Supporters of Egypt's new President Mohammed Mursi, of the Muslim Brotherhood, are in a standoff with generals who have ruled since the ouster of Hosni Mubarak. During a meeting with President Mursi, Secretary of State Hillary Clinton urged compromise and real politics, while also praising Egypt's military council for its interim leadership. Clinton aims to support Egypt's democratic transition while encouraging Mursi to address issues like the peace treaty with Israel and the protection of women and minorities.

Derek Bruder testified about a 1990 meeting with West Midlands Police officer Matthew Sawers in which Bruder claims he was pressured to revise his statement on the condition of 15-year-old Kevin Williams following the 1989 Hillsborough disaster. Bruder alleges Sawers asked him to speak to a pathologist from the coroner's office, who suggested that Kevin could not have been alive when Bruder attempted to revive him. Bruder maintains Sawers was dishonest with him and West Midlands Police deliberately attempted to modify his statement. The inquests about the 96 lives lost at the 1989 FA Cup semi-final between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest are set to resume on Monday.

The article discusses the journey of the British musical duo Oh Wonder, who experienced sudden fame after their self-released songs, including Body Gold, became an online phenomenon, eventually leading to a record deal and an extensive world tour. To maintain anonymity due to injury and their belief in "art over artist", they used a vocal technique where both musicians sing in unison, becoming known for their unique sound. Post-tour, they penned their upcoming album Ultralife, which they say reflects the ability of certain people to pull one out of difficult moments and into a positive, energetic state. The album is set to be released on July 14, 2017.

Chelsea took the lead against Stoke City when Bertrand Traore scored from 20 yards out, but the Potters equalised when Diouf headed in after Courtois failed to deal with a cross. Despite fielding a weakened lineup, both teams ended the game with a point each.

The research of William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu has led to the development of drugs that combat malaria, onchocerciasis (river blindness), and lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis), diseases affecting over 3.4 billion people worldwide. Their work has resulted in the development of ivermectin to combat roundworm parasites, as well as the discovery of artemisinin for malaria treatment. However, resistance to these drugs is emerging, necessitating ongoing research for new treatments.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation, led by Nelson Mandela's associates, reported concerns about President Jacob Zuma's use of power and wielding undue influence in government and key institutions by the Gupta family. This has led to allegations of bribery, abuse of power, and endangerment of the nation's democracy, according to the Foundation. These allegations center on the offer of influential government positions and business favors by the Gupta family, which the parties involved have denied. The Foundation's concerns come as a court delays the release of a report by former anti-corruption chief Thuli Madonsela investigating these allegations against Zuma.

Miranda, the comedian and actress, received positive reviews for her West End debut as the "clowny" Miss Hannigan in the musical Annie. The musical includes the songs "It's A Hard Knock Life," "Tomorrow," and "Easy Street."

Jonjo Shelvey contributed to both goals in a 2-1 Newcastle victory over West Ham, moving the Magpies up one place in the league. Despite missed opportunities in the first half, Newcastle held on for the win thanks to a crucial save from Rob Elliot in the 90th minute. Steve McClaren emerged victorious against former England manager Slaven Bilic. The reverse fixture earlier this season resulted in a West Ham win. Newcastle play Watford away on 23 January.

Supermarkets Morrisons, Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury's cut diesel prices by up to 2p per litre due to lower wholesale costs, potentially making diesel cheaper than petrol for the first time since 2001, according to Experian Catalyst analysis. The RAC suggests this trend is influenced by increased diesel supply from overseas refineries and a stronger pound against the US dollar.

The 70th UN General Assembly for African leaders is a meeting where diplomatic negotiations, shopping, immunity, and humanitarian concerns like hunger and poverty coexist. The SDGs, which tackle issues like poverty and hunger, were presented, but Southern Africa still grapples with food shortages. Despite criticisms, the UN remains a crucial tool for addressing the continent's hunger and food security challenges.

The police are warning about potentially deadly Superman logo pills containing PMMA still circulating, as experts warn not to assume a different logo means the drug is safe, and there's no reliable way to tell if a pill contains PMMA.

A former Leave.EU campaign chairman, Arron Banks, urged UKIP leader Paul Nuttall to involve ex-leader Nigel Farage, arguing that he is "our biggest asset." He also proposed strategies such as hiring a CEO from industry and creating policies based on public input. UKIP's MEP Patrick O'Flynn, who is also Nuttall's political advisor, has responded critically to suggestions of donor involvement in party leadership decisions.

The article discusses a service called Invisible Girlfriend/Boyfriend, where for a fee, you can create a fictional relationship on social media and receive texts, voicemails, etc. from a real person. The service, intended to provide companionship and/or create the illusion of a relationship, has had thousands of users worldwide.

Germany demonstrated formidable offensive play against Poland, led by Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, and Bastian Schweinsteiger. Occasional lapses in concentration by German players may present potential opportunities for Scotland in their upcoming match. The frequency of these lapses and any specific Polish players mentioned in the article are not explicitly stated.

In a Championship match, Tammy Abraham missed a crucial opportunity for Bristol City, but Sam Gallagher scored a late header for Blackburn Rovers to earn a 1-1 draw, leaving them two points from safety with three games remaining. Bristol City dominated the first 70 minutes but were unable to hold onto their lead, while Blackburn face Wolves, Aston Villa, and Brentford in their final three matches. The goal was Blackburn's first point in two games.

Scotland's number eight Strauss seeks to help Scotland coach Cotter win against Ireland in the upcoming Six Nations match, aiming to break their 13-year streak of losing the opening day fixture. Ireland, known for their strong set-piece play, is expected to provide a tough challenge for Scotland's inexperienced front-row.

Celtic's John Guidetti scored a free-kick after Pascali received a red card for pulling back Celtic's Stefan Scepovic, and Sceptovic added a second after the break, with Conor Brennan making several saves for Kilmarnock in their 2-0 defeat to Celtic.

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development study shows that, despite having high levels of test anxiety, bullying, and extensive internet use, Northern Irish students have an average life satisfaction score slightly below the OECD average, and have the lowest rate of bullying in the UK.

In an unexpected reversal, Palace, initially struggling against a dominant Everton side, fought back from a deficit to score three goals, taking control of the game. Everton refused to give up and scored a late penalty, but Palace held on for a 3-2 victory.

Freelance sports journalist Gary Carter, who was covering a rugby league match, suffered head injuries in an altercation in London and was admitted to the Royal London Hospital for surgery to remove a blood clot from his brain. His wife reported that he was heavily sedated due to swelling on the brain. A 35-year-old man has been charged with causing grievous bodily harm, and both a 22-year-old and another individual were arrested in connection with the incident. The England team and fellow sports figures offered their support and well wishes for a full recovery.

British artist Tinie Tempah, with seven number one singles in this decade, discusses his clutter-free London studio, showcasing his PlayStation 4 and affection for FIFA games. He details his two-year creative process for album "Youth," struggling with his perspective as a British rapper and losing touch with his roots. explains how reconnecting with friends and his past experiences fueled his latest work. Tinie Tempah's album "Youth" is slated for release on April 14th.

Mobile operators led by O2 and Vodafone are set to discuss with Ofcom and the Culture Secretary the acceleration of the allocation of spectrum for 4G networks, aiming to launch services and close the gap with market leader EE. The iPhone 5, available on all major networks, can only offer 4G speeds on EE's network, and the success of EE's 4G network depends on competitive pricing and the iPhone 5 market impact.

The Conservative government has decided to stop a policy offering a free school meal for every child in the first three years of primary school, causing concerns among teachers and school heads that it could have negative effects on students and schools, as well as on families struggling to afford school meals.

A shooting in a bar in central Tel Aviv left several civilians injured, with speculation of a potential link to organized crime or a hate crime. Israeli authorities are actively searching for the gunman, who is believed to be an Israeli Arab, amidst mounting violence between Israelis and Palestinians.

Musical artist Dean Owens discovered his great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona, a popular lion tamer who arrived in Inverness, Scotland in the late 19th Century with a dancing bear, was buried in Tomnahurich Cemetery following his death in 1917. His discovery influenced Owens' songwriting, particularly in the track 'Dora' from his Nashville-recorded album Into the Sea, which tells the story of his grandmother who grew up in a circus started by Salvona in Scotland. Local historians have uncovered more details about Salvona's life, including two marriages and the birth of at least 10 children.

At this year's Glastonbury music festival, sustainable, recycled stainless steel pint glasses were introduced as a move towards reducing waste and supporting the UK steel industry. These glasses were manufactured by APS in Birmingham using British recycled steel, although they are not easily identifiable as Glastonbury cups and can be difficult to throw effectively due to their unusual shape and lack of a lid. The use of these cups is seen as a step towards a larger push towards sustainability and reusable products at the festival, with the £5 deposit system encouraging people to hang onto them. Unfortunately, the production of steel does release pollutants, although it is still considered a greener option compared to plastic cups, which release additional toxic chemicals and take a long time to decompose in the environment.

A 15-year-old boy miraculously survived a banquet collapse during the Nepal earthquake by drinking water, many were rescued from the rubble, some suffered from waterborne illnesses, and frustration over the pace of relief efforts mounted in some rural areas, with the death toll rising to 6,130, over eight million people affected, and 70,000 houses destroyed. The UN supported the aid operation with search-and-rescue teams, aircraft, medical supplies, and communications equipment.

JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, and insurers Lloyd's of London and Royal London may relocate staff from London to Dublin, Frankfurt, Luxembourg, and Milan to mitigate potential Brexit-related disruptions, while the impact on Standard Chartered's UK staff would be "minimal."

Protestors in Ferguson, Missouri, clashed with police following the shooting of black teenager Michael Brown on August 9. Seven arrests were made during a protest and the US justice department is investigating the shooting. The officer involved, Darren Wilson, a six-year police veteran with no previous complaints, is under investigation, and the released CCTV footage has faced criticism from Brown's family. A peaceful rally led by Brown's family is planned for a later date.

Diane Abbott criticizes Theresa May's tenure as Home Secretary for allowing a reduction in police numbers, specifically community officers, potentially contributing to recent terrorist attacks. The Conservatives criticize Abbott's proposed security measures, while some experts dispute the connection between police cuts and terrorism.

The world champions, New Zealand, routed Wales 46-6 in the final Test, marking their 29th consecutive loss to the All Blacks, and their heaviest defeat since 2007. Despite the loss, coach Warren Gatland sees improvements for his team, particularly in areas like counter-attacking and collision dominance at the breakdown. Steve Hansen suggests that Wales' poor performance may have been influenced by the end of their season, and believes they will rebound in the Six Nations.

The Leviathan II whale-watching boat, operated by Jamie's Whaling Station and Adventure Centre, capsized in Canada on Sunday, killing five passengers, including a 17-year-old boy from Swindon, a 63-year-old man from Southampton, a 76-year-old man who had lived in Canada for many years, a 29-year-old woman living in Whistler, and another British woman. All five victims were on the open, upper deck of the boat and were not wearing life jackets. A 27-year-old Australian man is missing, and the Canadian government is investigating the cause of the accident. The Leviathan II has also been involved in a previous fatal accident in 1998.

Myanmar's President Thein Sein views a newly signed agreement as a necessary step towards a temporary ceasefire aimed at ending decades-long conflicts between the government and various rebel groups. However, not all key rebel groups, including the United Wa State Army (UWSA) and the Kachin Independence Organisation (KIO), have signed the agreement. The government hopes this agreement will serve as a first step in reaching political settlements ahead of general elections, despite concerns about future violations by the military and short-lived peace.

Facebook was ordered by the High Court in Northern Ireland to remove a page that exposed personal information and harassed a man with 15 convictions for sexual offences committed in the 1980s, due to the risk of infringing his human rights. However, the ruling does not suppress information about the man that is already in the public domain, and further steps are required to prevent further unlawful conduct towards the man on social networking sites pending the substantive trial of this action.

Apple is inviting publishers to join a new app service, which requires active opt-out to avoid having to indemnify Apple in case of legal issues and allowing Apple to place ads next to their content, with concerns raised that the opt-out approach amounts to presumed acceptance of the terms. The service, which will be categorized under Apple's marketing department, is due to launch later this year as part of iOS9.

The article discusses the varying levels of concern among residents of Guam, an important US military base and US territory home to about 6,000 troops and 165,000 civilians, in response to North Korean threats. Governor Eddie Baza Calvo has reassured the public of no immediate threat, but residents are preparing for possible escalation due to the island's proximity to North Korea and the volatile rhetoric between Kim Jong-un and President Trump. While some residents express concern, others view the situation as repetitive and see a sense of resignation.

Sentinel-1b, launched by a Soyuz rocket in French Guiana, will join Sentinel-1a in orbit to deliver radar imagery for various Earth-monitoring applications such as shipping lane pollution, iceberg surveillance, and land subsidence analysis. The European Union's Copernicus program utilizes data from multiple sources, including Sentinel-1b, to support various services such as air quality updates, crop-performance monitoring, water-resource management, and transport infrastructure planning. Sentinel-1b was the fourth satellite launched in the series, with more to follow, and it will take two weeks to reach its operational orbit, where it will undergo commissioning and calibration. The Microscope satellite, a fundamental physics experiment, was also deployed on the same flight to investigate the "equivalence principle."

The article suggests that the pound has recently strengthened due to the perceived possibility of a softer Brexit following Theresa May's upcoming general election, which could potentially give her more political leverage. This increased likelihood of a softer Brexit has boosted the pound, although it is also predicted to reduce the value of foreign earnings for UK companies causing the stock market to decline. Despite businesses being generally supportive of the election, there is uncertainty about whether May will actually pursue a softer Brexit.

A Czech hiker named Pavlina Pizova spent nearly a month alone in the New Zealand wilderness after her partner, Ondrej Petr, died following a slip on an ice slope during a hiking trip on the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park. She was found by a search team in early August, 2021 and was in reasonable health.

Elena, a Russian woman, faces a debt of over 1 million roubles, indicative of a larger pattern of personal debt in Moscow, amounting to over 1tn roubles nationwide. This situation, with millions of Russians struggling to pay their loans or mortgages, is exacerbated by a lack of financial education and the ease with which individuals borrowed money, a trend that started in the 1990s.

A suspect identified as James Holmes is accused of a deadly mass shooting at a Batman movie premiere, facing court hearings amidst mental health concerns, and Christian Bale is one of several Hollywood stars visiting hospitalized victims, with law enforcement showing support; however, the White House and Congress view this incident as not conducive for immediate gun control legislation.

The Art Recovery Group is combating the increase in illegally traded artifacts from Syria by maintaining a database to identify looted antiquities, verifying provenance information, notifying authorities, and collaborating with international governments on art crime prevention efforts, particularly focusing on resourcing and building up art crime units worldwide.

The Nuclear Accident Independent Investigation Commission's report found that the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster was a man-made disaster resulting from collusion between government, regulators, and plant operator Tepco, as well asdeep-rooted organizational, regulatory, and safety shortcomings in Japan's culture and systems, resulting in failures in emergency preparedness, response, evacuation, and public health protection.
